newsitem.title: USA: TWA crash investigators brief House panel on claims.
newsitem.headline: TWA crash investigators brief House panel on claims.

text.p: Federal investigators told a U.S. House of Representatives subcommittee on Wednesday that there was no evidence to support claims that a U.S. Navy missile shot down TWA Flight 800 off Long Island, New York, last year.

Lead investigator James Kallstrom, assistant director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation's New York office, and National Transportation Safety Board Director Jim Hall gave a closed-door briefing on the TWA investigation to members of the House Transportation subcommittee on aviation.

Subcommittee Chairman John Duncan, a Tennessee Republican, said through an aide that the NTSB, FBI and U.S. Navy investigators did a good job going through the evidence and putting to rest claims that the July 17, 1996, crash was caused by a missile fired during a Navy training exercise.
"They did a great job of dispelling a lot of the rumours that have been ongoing in this investigation," the aide said.

Investigators told the panel they found nothing to support claims by television correspondent Pierre Salinger that a U.S. Navy missile accidentally caused the Boeing 747 to explode in midair off New York's Long Island shortly after takeoff, killing all 230 people on board, the aide said.
Investigators know the centre fuel tank exploded, but have been unable to explain why.
